entities.summary: Tiberius Julius Candidus Capito (b. 50 CE) was a prominent entrepreneur and business leader of the Roman Empire during the Classical era, with known connections to religious figures and institutions. Capito was born into a wealthy family and began his career in trade and commerce, expanding his business interests throughout the Roman Empire. He was known for his innovative business practices, including the use of new financial instruments and his ability to navigate complex trade routes. Capito's success in business led to his appointment as a high-ranking official in the Roman administration, where he played a key role in shaping the empire's economic policies. Despite his significant influence, little is known about Capito's personal life, and his legacy has been largely overshadowed by that of his contemporaries. His impact on the development of the Roman Empire's economy and trade networks remains a topic of interest among historians.
